tcmvNext.label: 6 Oct TCMV: discussed, no vote; December meeting expected, vote not decided
tcmvNext.note: The 119th TCMV met on 6 October 2026. Its published draft agenda (DG GROW; draft dated ~11 September) listed only “Continuation of discussions on request of the Netherlands for an Art. 39 authorisation” (~25 min, 11:45–12:10), with no vote; press reports after the meeting (heise/dpa, TeslaNorth, 6 October) describe discussion only, no vote. The Commission's summary record of the 30 June TCMV meeting (published 16 October 2026; https://ec.europa.eu/transparency/comitology-register/screen/documents/118568/1) shows no vote. The Netherlands reported 40 million km driven, and its data put the system's speed adaptation at an average 4.4 km/h below the detected limit. Member states asked about the name, the permanent speed offset, over-the-air updates and bad weather; the Commission said the timeline depends on their satisfaction with the Dutch answers. As of 26 October no official readout of the 6 October meeting has been found. The next TCMV meeting is expected in December; whether it will hold a vote is not yet decided (earlier Electrek/Reuters reporting called December the earliest apparent opportunity and did not confirm a Commission vote date). The Norwegian Public Roads Administration (Statens vegvesen), on its page updated 29 October 2026, says the next meeting is in December 2026, that it is still not decided whether a vote will take place, and that the wording of any decision to be voted on is not settled (https://www.vegvesen.no/fag/trafikk/its-portalen/its-i-statens-vegvesen/metr/forerstottesystemer/).

sourcesNote: Sweden row updated 12 November 2026: Transportstyrelsen’s page on advanced driver-assistance systems, published 11 May 2026 and last changed 26 October 2026 (https://www.transportstyrelsen.se/sv/om-oss/det-har-ar-transportstyrelsen/forskning-och-innovation/automatiserade-vagtransporter/transportstyrelsens-syn-pa-avancerade-forarstodssystem-i-sverige/), says Sweden is analysing RDW’s 10 April 2026 provisional approval of Tesla FSD (Supervised), now Tesla Assisted Driving. A general approval cannot be given before the member-state vote, and before the system is judged to meet UN Regulation No. 171. Transportstyrelsen has allowed Tesla limited tests with trained test drivers on certain routes. General consumer activation is not yet permitted. If member states vote no, national permits are withdrawn; if they vote yes, a broader launch could be possible at the earliest in spring or summer 2027. That 2027 timing is Transportstyrelsen’s own estimate. Tesla Assisted Driving is a driver-assistance system and the driver stays legally responsible. Status stays in_review — not a national approval. Counts unchanged: eleven of 27; EU population share about 15.5%. The row now links to that page. This page stores one source URL per country, so the Riksdag written answer 2025/26:1000 (https://www.riksdagen.se/sv/dokument-och-lagar/dokument/skriftlig-fraga/sveriges-standpunkt-i-eu-gallande-behandling-av_hd111000/) is no longer the row link; it remains the Carlson source and is still linked in the speed-offset section. Finland row updated 11 November 2026: Traficom news release published 11 November 2026 at 07:53 Finnish time (https://www.traficom.fi/en/news/teslas-driver-assistance-system-now-permitted-finnish-roads) says that on 10 November 2026 Traficom recognised the provisional type-approval granted by the Dutch authority (RDW) for Tesla Assisted Driving, so it can be used as a driver assistance system in Finland and Tesla can immediately start offering it to customers. Recorded here as national recognition of that Dutch provisional approval under Article 39(5) of Regulation (EU) 2018/858 — approved (eleventh). Traficom stresses the driver remains fully responsible; says operation may be limited if cameras are covered by snow, slush or other dirt; says further changes to the system are expected before EU-wide approval; says EU-wide approval needs a TCMV vote, expected during the coming winter, taking effect about three weeks after a successful vote; and says national recognition does not bind Finland’s position in that vote. Reuters reported the release on 11 November 2026. Customer rollout to Finnish customers is not yet confirmed. EU population share: (64.4 + 5.6) / 450.2 ≈ 15.5%. Netherlands row and speed-offset FAQ updated 4 November 2026: RDW news of 3 November 2026 (https://www.rdw.nl/over-rdw/nieuws/2026/rdw-keurt-wijzigingen-aan-tesla-rijhulpsysteem-goed) approves Tesla’s “minor changes” for HW4 and later: maximum speed margin +10% (was +50%), default 0% at every start with other speed-related functions off, and the Tesla Assisted Driving name in the car and manual, delivered over the air. Existing type approval stays valid with no amendment or extension; RDW informed the nine recognising states; TCMV talks confidential and RDW declines comment. Status counts unchanged. Italy and Norway rows and the TCMV timing note updated 3 November 2026. Italy stays in_review with no date: Tesla has filed for recognition of the Dutch homologation; MIT said in July 2026 that the file is in analysis; no customer activation; the day of filing was not published. On 29 October 2026 Transport Minister Matteo Salvini posted that Italy supports a swift EU approval of Tesla Assisted Driving (https://x.com/matteosalvinimi/status/2115720560994836862). That is political support, not an Italian national approval. The row now links to that post. This page stores one source URL per country, so the July 2026 report (https://driveteslacanada.ca/news/tesla-fsd-italy-application-under-review/) is no longer the row link. Norway stays non_eu. The Norwegian Public Roads Administration (Statens vegvesen) updated its page on 29 October 2026 (https://www.vegvesen.no/fag/trafikk/its-portalen/its-i-statens-vegvesen/metr/forerstottesystemer/). Norway is in the EEA, takes part in TCMV without a vote, and follows EU type-approval through the EEA Agreement. The page says the next TCMV meeting is in December 2026, that it is not yet decided whether a vote will be held, and that the wording of any decision is not settled. Tesla has dropped its requested exemption from the maximum lateral-acceleration requirement. Counts unchanged: 10 of 27; EU population share 14.3%. Latvia row updated 26 October 2026: CSDD (Ceļu satiksmes drošības direkcija, Latvia’s type-approval authority) press release of 26 October 2026 recognises the Dutch RDW provisional approval under Article 39(5) of Regulation (EU) 2018/858 — approved (tenth). csdd.lv did not load in our checks; the release text is carried by Apollo.lv / TVNET, Kursors.lv and BB.LV, and Reuters reported Tesla’s announcement the same day. Tesla Europe posted on X on 26 October that rollout “begins soon”; customer rollout not yet confirmed. EU population share: (62.5 + 1.9) / 450.2 = 14.3%. Luxembourg row updated 21 October 2026: written answer of Mobility Minister Yuriko Backes to parliamentary question no. 4802 (20 October 2026, chd.lu) — not involved in the Dutch procedure; driver assistance, not automated driving; supports harmonised EU procedure; no national recognition (status unchanged). Slovakia row updated 19 October 2026: Ministerstvo dopravy SR press release of 16 October 2026 recognises the Dutch RDW provisional approval — approved (ninth); Tesla Europe posted on X on 16 October that rollout “begins soon”; Slovak media report a gradual over-the-air rollout. Germany row updated 7 October 2026: BMV statement of 6 October 2026 (support for EU-wide approval; max 10% speed tolerance agreed with Tesla; driver 100% responsible; Tesla offered “Tesla Assisted Driving” name) — no national approval. TCMV row updated 7 October 2026: 6 October meeting discussed the Dutch request without a vote; no official readout yet. Statuses from official notices. Croatia row updated 30 September 2026: Državni zavod za mjeriteljstvo (DZM, Croatian type-approval body) recognised the Dutch RDW provisional FSD (Supervised) approval (letter to Tesla Hrvatska, quoted by HINA / N1, 29 Sep ~17:10 CEST) under Regulation (EU) 2018/858; Tesla Europe X same morning secondary; no DZM press page found on dzm.gov.hr yet — letter via HINA wire. Rollout soon; confirm in the Tesla app. Jutarnji overclaims “fully autonomous” framing — do not cite that headline. TCMV row updated 28 September 2026: published draft agenda for the 119th TCMV (6 October 2026; DG GROW; draft ~11 September) lists only “Continuation of discussions on request of the Netherlands for an Art. 39 authorisation” (~25 min, 11:45–12:10) — Tesla not named, no vote; Electrek and Reuters 25 September and fsd-eu-tracker.de matched that discussions-only draft; those September reports treated December as the next meeting and did not confirm a vote date. Germany stays in_review from BMV Staatssekretär Christian Hirte’s written answer to MdB Maximilian Kneller (Frage Nr. 0121/September; letter 14 September 2026; Kneller X 23 September): KBA still evaluating RDW Article 39 file; Speed Offset talks with RDW and Tesla; October discussion hedge now aligned to the draft agenda’s discussions-only item. Czechia row updated 21 September 2026 from MDČR press release recognising Dutch RDW provisional FSD (Supervised) approval; ministry X (@min_dopravy) and Tesla Europe same morning secondary; Tesla Europe still “Rollout will begin soon” (no formal “now live for all CZ”); secondary Czech press claims of Prague unlocks do not replace a Tesla Europe universal-unlock notice. Spain row updated 17 September 2026: Tesla Europe (16 Sep) ~460,000 km company testing — not customer unlock. Slovenia: AVP temporary recognition 7 Sep; early SI unlocks reported (owner secondary); October TCMV vote language removed. Sweden: Riksdag written answer 2025/26:1000. Ireland: Irish Examiner 23 Sep quotes Tesla “working with authorities” / anticipating arrival — not unlock. Tracker is a third-party view, not scraped live by this site.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.blurb: Provisional EU type-approval under Article 39, valid in the Netherlands. First in Europe. Subscribe in the Tesla app. On 3 November 2026 the RDW approved Tesla’s changes (speed margin capped at +10%, default 0% at start, Tesla Assisted Driving name); the approval itself is unchanged.

countries.name: Lithuania
countries.authority: Ministry of Transport and Communications + LTSA
countries.blurb: National recognition of the Dutch provisional approval under Article 39(5).

countries.name: Estonia
countries.blurb: Recognises the Dutch type-approval. Official page classifies it as SAE Level 2.

countries.name: Denmark
countries.blurb: Accepts the Dutch provisional approval after its own document review. States the six-month lapse rule in public.

countries.name: Belgium
countries.blurb: Annick De Ridder (Flemish Minister of Mobility) signed recognition of the Dutch Article 39 file on 10 June 2026. Reporting, including VRT, says a regional type-approval signature has nationwide effect.

countries.name: Germany
countries.blurb: Germany’s Federal Transport Ministry (BMV) said on 6 October 2026 that Minister Steffen Bilger will work for a timely EU-wide approval, after talks with Tesla in September. The BMV says the two agreed the system may exceed the speed limit slightly, by a maximum of 10%, that the driver stays 100% responsible, and that Tesla offered to rename the system “Tesla Assisted Driving” (the BMV called the name “FSD” somewhat misleading). Tesla made that rename in Europe on 9 October 2026. Germany supports continuing the EU procedure. This is not a German national approval and sets no date. Separately, dpa/heise quote Bilger saying Germany would discuss national options if an EU agreement fails. The KBA is still assessing the RDW file. Write for a TCMV yes.

countries.name: France
countries.blurb: Tabarot declined national recognition of the current product on 22 July 2026 and wants an EU-wide framework. Not a pending rubber-stamp.

countries.name: Italy
countries.authority: Ministero delle Infrastrutture e dei Trasporti (DG Motorizzazione)
countries.blurb: Tesla has filed for recognition of the Dutch homologation. MIT said in July 2026 that the file is in analysis. No customer activation. The day of filing was not published. On 29 October 2026, Transport Minister Matteo Salvini publicly backed a swift EU approval of Tesla Assisted Driving. That is political support, not a national approval.

countries.name: Spain
countries.authority: Ministerio de Industria y Turismo + DGT
countries.blurb: Reported 23 July 2026: Minister Hereu said Spain would not unilaterally adopt the Dutch file and is coordinating with the Commission, DGT and UN. Tesla Europe (16 September 2026) reported ~460,000 km of FSD (Supervised) testing in Spain over two years — company testing under DGT / ES-AV, not customer unlock / not national recognition of the Dutch file. The ministerial reply was not found on mintur.gob.es.

countries.name: Poland
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask the ministry for a public Article 39(5) position and a TCMV line.

countries.name: Romania
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask the ministry for a public position.

countries.name: Czechia
countries.blurb: MDČR recognised the Dutch RDW provisional FSD (Supervised) approval on 21 September 2026, joining NL and five other European states. Tesla Europe announced the same morning; rollout will begin soon — confirm in the Tesla app.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.blurb: No customer approval. Trafikverket’s 30 April TCMV letter recommends a no unless Speed Offset is removed. Infrastrukturminister Carlson’s written answer (letter 31 August, published 1 September 2026) restates a union-wide ADAS ambition and still takes Trafikverket into account. That is not a locked TCMV yes. Transportstyrelsen (page updated 26 Oct 2026): Tesla may run limited tests with trained test drivers; consumer activation is not allowed before the EU vote; even after a yes, it says a broader Swedish launch is possible at the earliest in spring or summer 2027.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask for a public Article 39(5) decision and a TCMV line.

countries.name: Greece
countries.blurb: Ministry said it would bring forward a bill to recognise the Dutch approval. No confirmation the bill was enacted. Do not treat Greece as approved.

countries.name: Hungary
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask for a public position.

countries.name: Austria
countries.blurb: Named by Germany’s BMV (Hirte, 25 August 2026) among Member States that have registered further examination need at TCMV. That is not a national customer approval and not a published yes/no.

countries.name: Bulgaria
countries.blurb: Named by Germany’s BMV (Hirte, 25 August 2026) among Member States that have registered further examination need at TCMV. That is not a national customer approval and not a published yes/no.

countries.name: Finland
countries.blurb: On 10 November 2026 Traficom recognised the provisional type-approval granted by the Dutch authority (RDW) for Tesla Assisted Driving (news release published 11 November 2026). That is national recognition of the Dutch provisional approval under Article 39(5) of Regulation (EU) 2018/858. Traficom says the driver remains fully responsible, and that snow, slush or other dirt on the cameras can limit the system. This recognition does not bind Finland’s position in the TCMV vote. EU-wide approval still needs that vote. Customer rollout in Finland is not yet confirmed.

countries.name: Slovakia
countries.blurb: Ministerstvo dopravy SR recognised the Dutch RDW provisional FSD (Supervised) approval on 16 October 2026 (ministry press release). Transport Minister Jozef Ráž: “Za jazdu je stále plne zodpovedný vodič” (the driver remains fully responsible). Tesla Europe posted on 16 October 2026 that the Slovak rollout “begins soon”; Slovak media (Zamerané, 18 October) report that some owners could switch it on the same day and that the over-the-air update is arriving gradually — confirm in the Tesla app.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.blurb: Named by Germany’s BMV (Hirte, 25 August 2026) among Member States that have registered further examination need at TCMV. Irish Examiner (23 September 2026) quotes Tesla saying it is “working with authorities” in Ireland toward FSD (Supervised) regulatory approval and “anticipating the arrival … in due course” — company statement, not a national customer unlock. Left-hand traffic is an extra technical issue.

countries.name: Croatia
countries.blurb: DZM (Croatian type-approval body) recognised the Dutch RDW provisional FSD (Supervised) approval on 29 September 2026 (letter to Tesla Hrvatska, quoted by HINA / N1). Tesla Europe announced the same morning; rollout will begin soon — confirm in the Tesla app. No DZM press page located on dzm.gov.hr yet.

countries.name: Slovenia
countries.blurb: AVP confirmed temporary recognition of the Dutch provisional FSD (Supervised) type approval (7 September 2026; AVP notice 8 September). Driver assistance, not autonomy. Early SI customer unlocks and first drives reported around 10–11 September 2026 (owner posts, secondary — e.g. Jan Skočaj; Igor Vovk). Confirm in the Tesla app; Tesla Europe’s 7 September line was still “Rollout will begin soon,” with no formal “now live for all SI” company notice. EU-wide decision still pending; the published 119th TCMV draft agenda (6 October) lists discussions only (no vote); the next TCMV meeting is expected in December, and whether it will hold a vote is not yet decided.

countries.name: Latvia
countries.blurb: CSDD recognised the Dutch RDW provisional FSD (Supervised) approval on 26 October 2026 (CSDD press release, carried by Apollo.lv / TVNET). CSDD describes Tesla Assisted Driving as a Level 2 driver-assistance system: the driver stays fully responsible and must watch the road, and snow, mud, road salt or gravel roads can limit it. The decision follows the Ministry of Economics’ September informative report (TAP 26-TA-2030). Tesla Europe posted on 26 October 2026 that the Latvian rollout “begins soon”; customer rollout not yet confirmed — confirm in the Tesla app.

countries.name: Cyprus
countries.blurb: Left-hand traffic; no published process.

countries.name: Luxembourg
countries.blurb: No national recognition. Minister Backes wrote to Parliament on 20 October 2026 that Luxembourg was not involved in the Dutch procedure, calls the system driver assistance under permanent driver supervision (not automated driving), and backs a harmonised EU procedure with rigorous safety assessment. Her 25 June 2026 answer said Luxembourg waits for the EU (TCMV) decision.
countries.sourceLabel: Chambre des Députés, written answer 20 Oct 2026

countries.name: Malta
countries.blurb: Left-hand traffic; no published process.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.blurb: Cannot use Article 39(5). Separate GB type-approval. R171 Series 02 is the realistic UN path. Not approved.

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.blurb: Applies R171 as a 1958 party; cannot accept the Dutch Article 39 file. Ride-alongs are not an approval.

countries.name: Norway
countries.blurb: Norway is in the EEA. It takes part in TCMV but has no vote, and it follows EU type-approval through the EEA Agreement. The Norwegian Public Roads Administration (Statens vegvesen), updated 29 October 2026, says the next TCMV meeting is in December 2026 and that it is not yet decided whether that meeting will hold a vote. The wording of any decision is not settled. Tesla has dropped its requested exemption from the maximum lateral-acceleration requirement. Statens vegvesen also expects Tesla to adjust speed-limit adaptation. It is not considering an earlier introduction in Norway while the system does not meet UN Regulation No. 171. Tesla Norway may use three modified vehicles for internal testing; customer demonstrations are not yet allowed.
